claims.claim: T-26271's CI diff failures ('argocd app diff' failing with missing-permissions after 'we recently enabled the sync impersonation flag') are explained by RFC-001's design: with application.sync.impersonation.enabled, operations run as the AppProject's destinationServiceAccounts identity rather than the broad cluster Secret credential the reporter is chasing, and that narrower service account cannot dry-run apply cluster-scoped RBAC resources.

T-28695 documents the inverse gap in RFC-001's decoupling: sync honors destinationServiceAccounts impersonation but the application-controller Server-Side Diff path still runs as the cluster Secret credential, forcing unbounded real 'patch' grants onto deliberately least-privilege external-cluster credentials — the exact 'large attack surface' on the standing credential that RFC-001's impersonation was meant to retire is instead widened to keep diffs working.

RFC-001 commits that 'The feature can be enabled/disabled only at the system level. Once enabled/disabled, it is applicable to all Argo CD Applications', but the platform sync call decided impersonation rollout 'goes behind a per-project flag, not fleet-wide' — the decided rollout model requires a per-project control the design explicitly does not provide.

The strategy roadmap states 'Deletion of generated Applications is explicitly out of scope for rollout orchestration: ordered or automated deletion of ApplicationSet children will not be implemented. Teardown remains a manual operator action', while the Progressive Sync Deletion PRD's goal is exactly that: a deletionOrder field (AllAtOnce/Reverse) that automates ordered deletion of ApplicationSet children. Both commitments cannot hold; note-2 flags the disagreement as needing an owner, undecided.

The PRD asserts 'No immediate Risks to consider' for deletionOrder, but T-28511 is field evidence against the Reverse semantics the PRD specifies ('Waits for one application to be fully deleted before moving onto the next'): a child app stuck Progressing makes that wait never complete, and the controller loops deleting/re-creating — an incident severe enough that the runbook now mandates switching to AllAtOnce before any manual child deletion.

RFC-002's design guarantees every dry commit produces a fresh hydrated commit on the syncSource branch, and T-27949's pilot reports each such hydrated commit 'is picked up as a source change' that restarts the RollingSync wave; combining the hydrator with progressive sync therefore restarts rollouts on every hydration cycle, and the incident review's interim rule (hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until a debounce exists) is recorded nowhere in either design document.

T-27875 shows apps with automated sync (without selfHeal) stall OutOfSync indefinitely when a new commit lands while a sync is in progress; RFC-002's hydrator makes exactly that pattern routine by pushing machine-generated commits to the syncSource branch on every dry change, so hydrator-managed branches are disproportionately exposed to the auto-sync stall.

RFC-002 introduces a component that pushes to git via a repository-write secret, and T-28239 records that these hydrated commits are unsigned — so if signature verification is enforced on the hydrated branch, Argo CD rejects its own output, and until commit signing ships an auditor cannot distinguish the hydrator bot's writes from any other holder of the push credential on the branch that is the deployed source of truth.

T-27327 proposes that rollback 'directly updates the sync branch (bypassing the staging branch)' in both hydrator modes, which contradicts RFC-002's core opinion that 'every change to an application's desired state must originate from a commit to a single GitOps repository' flowing through the push-to-stage integration point built for promotion systems — rollback becomes a sanctioned write path around the very stage gate the RFC provides.

T-26443's stale-manifest syncs occur only in push-to-stage mode because 'the external promoter has not yet moved the fresh manifests to the deployment branch' — and note-1 records that this promoter 'is still the shell script, nobody owns it', parked without an owner; RFC-002's push-to-stage mode explicitly 'relies on some external system' that is currently unowned and already implicated in a filed defect.

T-27833's proposal (split resource handling so namespaces stay with the control-plane SA while the impersonated SA syncs everything else, stripping 'kind: namespace' from it) and T-9095's ask (respect cluster K8s RBAC instead of duplicated Argo-specific RBAC) both converge on RFC-001's access model of kubernetes-native RBAC via destinationServiceAccounts; under that model the acting identity becomes the destination service account and, per RFC-001, the kubernetes audit trail captures both actual and impersonated user — so access review for these asks must follow the per-namespace service accounts, not the Argo CD control-plane credential.

T-24578's motivation — 'control the destroy order of Application creation/deletion' because ApplicationSets shadow deletion ordering — is the same underlying need the PRD's deletionOrder: Reverse addresses; neither document cites the other, and T-24578's proposed hydrator-based workaround becomes unnecessary if the PRD ships.

RFC-002 resolves external Helm values by recommending 'the umbrella chart approach', judging 'the simplification is worth the cost of convenience', but T-24417 reports that switching to helm dependencies 'makes it difficult to use with ApplicationSets to control the chart version across environments' — field evidence against the assumption the RFC's Handling External Values Files decision rests on.

T-28927 scopes promoting Progressive Sync to Stable while the observability needed to validate it is still an open request: T-27846 asks for the basic progressive-sync metrics ('my sync is not starting, why/which Applications is it waiting for?') and T-27949's live failure was invisible because 'ApplicationSet controller logs were at warn level, so no relevant progressive-sync transition logs were emitted' — the feature is being matured before its failure modes are measurable in production.

Note-1's standing rule that 'nobody flips it on a project until the diff story is fixed' gates more than the impersonation rollout itself: T-27833's namespace-restriction ask and T-28695's least-privilege external-cluster posture both depend on impersonation being enabled, so every workstream built on destinationServiceAccounts is blocked behind the unfixed diff identity gap reported in T-26271 and T-28695.

proposals.change: Record the root cause: with sync impersonation enabled, the diff runs as the destination service account, which lacks patch on cluster-scoped resources; the broad cluster Secret credential is not the identity in play, so stop investigating it.
proposals.citedLine: the CI diff failures (the missing-permissions one, T-26271) got root-caused on the call: with impersonation on, diff runs as the destination service account which doesn't hold patch on cluster-scoped stuff. someone should note the root cause on that ticket so the reporter stops chasing the cluster secret.

proposals.change: Record that hydrator rollback work is deprioritized to next quarter and the dev pair has moved to the progressive sync deletion work.
proposals.citedLine: hydrator rollback work (the history & rollback ticket, T-27327) is deprioritized to next quarter. dev pair moves to the progressive sync deletion loop instead. ticket should say so.

proposals.change: Record the reproduction (staging, reverse deletion order) and the interim mitigation: per the incident runbook, switch the ApplicationSet to AllAtOnce deletion before manually deleting any child application, until the controller fix lands.
proposals.citedLine: the delete/recreate loop (T-28511) reproduced in staging with the reverse deletion order. mitigation for now: incident runbook says switch the ApplicationSet to AllAtOnce deletion before deleting any child app by hand. that's the operational rule until the controller fix lands — worth remembering as a standing practice.

proposals.change: Record the confirmed mechanism (each hydrator push restarts the rolling sync wave) and the interim restriction from the incident review: hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until a debounce exists.
proposals.citedLine: the wave-restart thing on hydrated repos: we confirmed each hydrator push restarts the rolling sync wave. interim call from the review: hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until there's a debounce. the pilot ticket (T-27949) should carry that restriction so the next team doesn't trip it.

deltas.body: Impersonation rollout goes behind a per-project flag, not fleet-wide, and no project enables it until the diff identity problem is fixed.
deltas.citedLine: impersonation rollout: we decided it goes behind a per-project flag, not fleet-wide. nobody flips it on a project until the diff story is fixed. that's a real decision, not a maybe.

deltas.body: Standing operational rule: before manually deleting any child Application of a progressive-sync ApplicationSet, switch the ApplicationSet's deletion to AllAtOnce; this holds until the controller fix lands.
deltas.citedLine: mitigation for now: incident runbook says switch the ApplicationSet to AllAtOnce deletion before deleting any child app by hand. that's the operational rule until the controller fix lands — worth remembering as a standing practice.

deltas.body: Standing restriction: hydrator pilot repositories must not use progressive sync until a debounce for hydrator-push wave restarts exists.
deltas.citedLine: interim call from the review: hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until there's a debounce. the pilot ticket (T-27949) should carry that restriction so the next team doesn't trip it.
